verdict.root_cause: No root cause is established by this board. Span-derived metrics do not exist for nginx-web-server or compose-post-service in either the onset or baseline window because neither emits traces that become metrics [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_00357570b0e6], which makes the empty Tempo result [tr_ce237924350e] the expected baseline for an uninstrumented service rather than a symptom of silence. Both Loki queries used guessed pod-name regexes that were never validated and returned empty results carrying a truncation flag [tr_c626ef4ef205][tr_4b6926841b8a], so that silence cannot be read as the service writing nothing. The only positive evidence is a three-second burst by platform-automation about six minutes before the 07:09:07 alert in which the nginx workload container, the nginx-thrift ConfigMap and the nginx-thrift Service were all created for the first time [tr_1808ab6d2147] - a bootstrap sequence, not a regression from a healthy baseline. That tells us nginx began serving against never-exercised routing config; it does not name what is failing now.
verdict.reasoning: Four of six dispatches returned nothing, and two of those nothings are explained by instrument coverage rather than by the incident [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_00357570b0e6]. Because those services emit no traces, the total absence of spans [tr_ce237924350e] is consistent with health, freeze, partition or error alike and discriminates nothing. The log silence [tr_c626ef4ef205][tr_4b6926841b8a] is similarly unusable: the specialists flagged that the selector may simply not match any running pod, and the results were marked truncated despite being empty. That leaves only the change record [tr_1808ab6d2147], which is evidence of an act, not of a mechanism - and its own specialist ruled out config regression, staged rollout, human edit, upstream repointing and restart-from-prior-revision. Naming any fault class on this basis would be classifying by the upstream act rather than by what the service is doing wrong, so the honest verdict is unknown with the investigation pointed at validating pod identity and finding a non-span signal.
open_questions: Do nginx-thrift and compose-post-service pods actually exist and are they Running? The Loki selectors were unvalidated regexes, so emptiness may be a label mismatch rather than a silent service.
What do nginx access/error logs show via a relaxed selector or an nginx exporter, since span metrics are structurally unavailable for this service?
Did the 07:02 bootstrap complete successfully - did the container reach Ready, and does the freshly created nginx-thrift ConfigMap name upstreams that actually resolve?

alternatives.root_cause: The freshly created nginx-thrift ConfigMap names upstreams that do not resolve, so nginx cannot route any request.
alternatives.why_not: Nothing read the ConfigMap's contents; the change record shows only that it was created. There is no prior version to revert to and no logged upstream error naming a wrong address or port.

alternatives.root_cause: The nginx process is stopped while its socket still accepts, so callers hang and the service writes nothing.
alternatives.why_not: The silence that would support this is not probative: traces are absent because the service is uninstrumented [tr_81d3c68dcd9a], and the log emptiness rests on an unvalidated selector with a truncation flag [tr_c626ef4ef205].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric or log stream should be observed as a result of this proposal. The next observable step is diagnostic, not remedial: a pod listing for the social-network namespace and a relaxed Loki selector (namespace-only, or label-based rather than guessed pod-name regex) would show whether nginx-thrift and compose-post-service pods exist, are Running, and are shipping any lines at all. That query returning named, running pods with log output - or returning no pods at all - is the observation that would let a real remediation be chosen.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the incident is in fact an ongoing hard outage that any of the three available actions would clear, and the delay costs availability. The observation that would show that: a relaxed-selector Loki query or nginx exporter surfacing a repeating upstream error (connection refused / host not found naming a nginx-thrift upstream), or a pod listing showing nginx-web-server in CrashLoopBackOff with a climbing restart count. Either would meet restart_service's precondition (process state) or point at the freshly created ConfigMap's upstream names, and the proposal should be reopened immediately. Note also that the effect of any fix here is hard to observe: span metrics are structurally absent for both nginx-web-server and compose-post-service [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_00357570b0e6], so error-ratio recovery cannot be measured - confirmation would have to come from access logs or an exporter, which is itself a reason not to act blind.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued outage if one is in progress. The risk of the alternative - acting anyway - is concrete and is why I decline: rollback_image has no prior image tag because the workload is recorded as first created, not redeployed [tr_1808ab6d2147], so it would redeploy to nothing; revert_config has no prior configuration because the nginx-thrift ConfigMap and Service were created rather than updated and no earlier version exists in the 24h window [tr_1808ab6d2147], so a revert would delete or blank working-or-not routing config with no known-good state to return to; restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and every process-state signal on this board is unavailable-or-unvalidated rather than negative [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_ce237924350e][tr_c626ef4ef205][tr_4b6926841b8a], so a restart would be a coin flip that destroys the current container state irreversibly and erases exactly the startup evidence needed to answer whether the 07:02 bootstrap completed.
proposal.blast_radius: None, since nothing is executed. Had an action been taken on nginx-web-server, it is the ingress for this slice and its callers are every external client of the social-network frontend; compose-post-service, home-timeline-service and user-timeline-service sit behind it and would see traffic stop for the duration of any container recreate. A restart of nginx-web-server in particular is irreversible per the action's own terms and would be visible to every user-facing request path at once.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on the front-door service with no open incidents to attribute it to cannot be dismissed, even though only the edge service has alerted so far. Nothing in the single-seed pattern points to a specific fault class yet.
